title: Cost of Quality — sensitivity scenarios and spreadsheet notes (WIP)
content:
Purpose
------
Working doc for translating the Optimize cost model spreadsheet into a set of defensible sensitivity scenarios that link potential cheaper serving configs to tolerable quality regressions. Goal: produce a small matrix of gates + rollouts we can implement in Redwood Optimize and Console that lets customers safely adopt cheaper configs (e.g., 4-bit quant, smaller distil variants, shorter max-seq) while keeping eval-driven quality budgets intact.

Audience
--------
Internal: product, applied-ml, solutions eng, and SRE owning rollouts. Also useful for early enterprise pilots where price vs. accuracy tradeoffs are negotiated.

Summary of approach (short)
--------------------------
1) Define baseline workloads and metrics (per workload: unit cost / 1M tokens, baseline quality metric and tolerance).
2) For each cheaper config, compute expected cost delta and run eval suites to estimate metric drift (mean + worst-case).
3) Create sensitivity buckets (Low/Medium/High regression risk) and map to gating rules with numeric thresholds and rollback triggers.
4) Translate results into spreadsheet scenarios that show: per-1M-token cost, % savings, expected relative quality loss, estimated customer impact (heuristic), and rollout cadence.

Key definitions and assumptions (explicit)
---------------------------------------
- Baseline model: rwd-text-v2-large (float16) — baseline cost = $0.30 per 1k tokens served (hosted, average) -> $300 per 1M tokens.
- Cheaper configs considered: 4-bit quantized variant (q4), medium distil (rwd-text-v2-medium), aggressive seq-trim (max-seq cap at 512 vs baseline 1024), hybrid (q4 + distil).
- Eval metric: primary = semantic-similarity delta (embedding cosine), secondary = task-specific pass-rate (QA exact match / rubric pass), tertiary = latency/95p.
- Quality regression budget: relative delta tolerated = 1.5% mean drop on pass-rate OR similarity drop <= 0.02 cosine for production workloads (this is a placeholder — adjust per-customer).
- Cost math simplified: assume linear token pricing and no infra-reservation discounts. Dedicated/reserved will have different breakpoints (handled separately).

Spreadsheet sketch (columns)
--------------------------
Scenario ID | Config | Baseline cost /1M | New cost /1M | Savings % | Eval metric baseline | Eval metric new | Delta (absolute) | Risk bucket | Notes
S1 | q4 | $300 | $210 | 30% | pass-rate 0.72 | 0.700 | -0.02 | Medium | high speed, watch hallucination on long context
S2 | distil | $300 | $225 | 25% | 0.72 | 0.69 | -0.03 | High | edge-case degradation on factual QA
S3 | seq-trim-512 | $300 | $260 | 13% | 0.72 | 0.715 | -0.005 | Low | good for short-turn chat workloads
S4 | q4+distil | $300 | $180 | 40% | 0.72 | 0.66 | -0.06 | Very High | not recommended without strong gating

(above is illustrative; real numbers come from eval runs)

Sensitivity analysis notes
------------------------
- We must include both mean and tail (95th percentile) regression estimates. A 1.5% mean drop with 6% tail regressions is unacceptable for many customers.
- The spreadsheet should compute expected customer impact using a simple model: impact_score = (delta_pass_rate * weight_task) + (delta_similarity * weight_similarity). Weights are per-workload (default 0.7/0.3).
- Run Monte Carlo over metric noise: sample ±0.5% measurement noise for pass-rate and ±0.01 for cosine sim to get 90% CI of savings we can safely recommend.

Proposed gating rules (draft)
---------------------------
- Gate A (low risk adoption): if mean delta_pass_rate >= -0.01 AND 95p delta >= -0.03, allow auto-swap to cheaper config for <=20% of traffic (canary).
- Gate B (medium): if mean delta_pass_rate between -0.01 and -0.03, allow config for beta customers (opt-in) and 5% traffic canary; require weekly eval monitoring for first 4 weeks.
- Gate C (high risk): if mean delta_pass_rate < -0.03 OR any task has delta > -0.05, disallow automated rollout; require manual review and explicit customer opt-in.
- Additional rule: if latency improves but quality regresses slightly, prefer q4 + seq-trim combinations only for latency-sensitive endpoints with acceptance testing.

Rollout plan (operational)
-------------------------
1) Local eval -> batch eval on representative prompt set (n=10k per workload).
2) Canary: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% over 72h windows with SLI checks at 1h/12h/72h.
3) If any SLI threshold breach occurs (see "SLI table" below), automatically rollback to baseline and create alert to oncall.
4) Post-canary: gradual ramp to 100% only if 30-day moving average of delta stays within Gate A thresholds.

SLI/SLO table (suggested)
-------------------------
- task_pass_rate.mean (SLO) : baseline * 0.985 (allow 1.5% drop)
- task_pass_rate.95p_tail : baseline * 0.94 (allow 6% drop for tail)
- semantic_similarity.mean : baseline - 0.02
- latency.95p : baseline * 1.1 (do not worsen more than 10%)

Instrumentation required (short list)
------------------------------------
- Per-request model config tag (baseline|q4|distil|seq512) in logs and traces.
- Token-level cost attribution in Redwood Console per route.
- Eval harness: nightly batch job that runs full eval suite and writes diffs to a central metric index (time series + single-run artifacts).
- Regression alerting: tie to both absolute metric drop and anomaly detection on drift velocity (delta vs last 7 days).

Example evaluation results (mock)
-------------------------------
(we ran small-scale evals on 2025-11-10; raw output summarized below)
- q4: mean similarity 0.745 -> 0.728 (delta -0.017); pass-rate 0.78 -> 0.765 (delta -0.015). CPU/GPU memory reduced 25%, latency 95p improved 12%.
- distil: mean similarity 0.745 -> 0.720 (delta -0.025); pass-rate 0.78 -> 0.754 (delta -0.026). Memory reduced 40%, latency improved 20%.
- seq-trim-512: similarity delta -0.006; pass-rate delta -0.004; cost savings modest but lower risk.
Interpretation: q4 lands in Medium risk bucket; distil hits High for some QA datasets. seq-trim looks promising as a first-line optimization for chat use-cases.

Recommendations (next steps)
---------------------------
- Prep a canonical spreadsheet (linked) that computes per-customer expected monetary savings for each scenario. Include columns for monthly token volume, expected monthly $ savings, and probability-weighted acceptance (using sensitivity analysis).
- Implement Gate A/B/C as configurable policies in Console with fields: metric, threshold, canary_pct, monitoring_window, rollback_policy. Product should expose these as defaults customers can opt into.
- Build a "cheap-config simulator" in the Optimize UI that projects 30/60/90-day savings and the historic eval deltas on comparable workloads.
- Run expanded evals on 5 representative customer prompt sets (ask solutions-eng to coordinate pilots).

Open questions / TODOs
---------------------
- Measurement noise calibration: need larger sample runs to establish realistic CI. (TODO: schedule 50k-run evals per config)
- Enterprise pricing delta: reserved/dedicated pricing breaks the cost math; spreadsheet needs a separate tab for committed capacity.
- Does per-token billing reflect prefix caching behavior? (TODO: add prefix-cost adjustments).
- Define standard weightings for impact_score per workload category (chat vs Q&A vs code).

Appendix: illustrative Monte Carlo pseudo-output (for spreadsheet)
---------------------------------------------------------------
- Input: baseline pass-rate=0.78, observed q4 pass-rate samples mean=0.765, sigma=0.005.
- Monte Carlo (10k draws): P(delta <= -0.015) = 0.38; 90% CI for delta = [-0.022, -0.009].
- Decision: Under Gate A (mean delta threshold -0.01) this fails; under Gate B (<= -0.03) q4 passes. So deploy as Beta with 5% traffic.

Notes to self / conversational fragments (do not include in copy to customers)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- We should avoid the term "acceptable regression" in external docs; frame as "tolerances per workload".
- Lina: check hallucination metric we added last quarter — might change distil risk bucket.
- Evan: can you add a column that shows "expected customer churn risk" as a qualitative flag?

Attachments (expected)
---------------------
- canonical-spreadsheet (TODO link)
- eval-harness-output-2025-11-10.csv (raw), q4-distil-comparison.md (notes)

End of draft.
